# 05. Golden dataset (generated by the agent)

Labels derive from case construction and mechanical checks. A second model flags cross-check disagreements; cases with unresolved disagreements stay outside the evaluation dataset.

## The one rule: label by construction

A label comes from how the case was built, never from asking a model whether code looks vulnerable. If a flaw is inserted into a clean function, its file, line, category and quote are known because you inserted them. If a bug is a mutation that existing tests catch, a failing test proves it.

## Base code

Write three small sample applications under `evals/sample_repos/`, each with a real test suite that passes: for example a note-taking API with a SQLite layer, a URL-shortener service, and a CSV report tool. Each has about 300 to 600 lines across 6 to 10 files, uses realistic patterns (database access, subprocess use, file paths, HTTP calls, config, logging, authentication checks), is licensed MIT, and is committed with its tests. These are the base code for most cases. Real open-source repositories are an optional extension, only if licenses are permissive and network access exists; record them in the manifest.

## Case sources

| Source | How it is made | How the label is known | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| seeded | take a clean function from a sample repo; the generator inserts one flaw from the taxonomy as a small diff | we inserted it | security reviewer, scanners, end-to-end recall |
| hard_negative | code that looks risky but is safe: parameterized queries, fake keys in test fixtures, secrets read from environment, subprocess with constant argument list and no shell | safe by construction | precision, skeptic |
| presumed_clean | benign PRs on the sample repos: refactors, small features with tests, docs; validated by passing tests and quiet static tools | presumed clean (flag in provenance) | false-positive rate |
| mutation | small mutation (flip comparison, off-by-one, drop null check, swallow exception) of a function that has tests; keep only mutations that make an existing test fail | a failing test | correctness reviewer |
| test_gap | PRs changing logic with no test change, versus with tests added | file paths | test reviewer |
| injection | wrap existing cases with attacker text in the placements from `04-evaluation.md` | metamorphic: decision must equal the unwrapped case | robustness |
| variant | rename variables, reformat, reorder files, add harmless comments | same label as the original | consistency |
| verifier_attack | break real findings: change the quote, shift lines, invent evidence ids | known fabricated | verifier |
| reversed_fix (optional) | published security advisory with a fix commit, fix reverse-applied | advisory plus fix location | realistic recall; only if network and token available |

## Taxonomy to seed

Security (12): hardcoded_secret, sql_injection, command_injection, path_traversal, unsafe_deserialization, ssrf, weak_crypto, tls_verification_disabled, xss, missing_authorization, insecure_randomness, sensitive_data_in_logs.
Correctness (6): off_by_one, wrong_condition, missing_null_check, resource_leak, swallowed_exception, wrong_default.
Test gaps (3): missing_test, test_weakened, assertion_removed.
Difficulty: obvious (visible in the hunk), subtle (needs a few lines of context), context_dependent (needs a caller or config).

## Case file format

Each case is a folder `evals/datasets/<version>/cases/<id>/` with `case.yml` and `change.diff`.

```yaml
id: sec-sqli-0007
source: seeded
split: dev                 # computed from the id hash (DECISIONS #19), never hand-set
tier: standard             # canary, standard or hard
difficulty: obvious
repo_snapshot: sample_notes_api@<git sha>
expected_decision: block
must_catch: true
findings:
  - category: sql_injection
    severity: critical
    file: app/db/users.py
    line_start: 41
    line_end: 42
    quote: the exact inserted line
provenance:
  generated_by: <model name or template>
  validators_passed: [parses, applies_cleanly, line_in_diff, quote_on_line, static_tool_agrees, cross_check_agrees]
```

`manifest.json` lists every case id with a content hash, counts per source and category, and version notes.

## Dataset factory (`evals/factory/`, its own small LangGraph)

```
pick_base_code -> seed_issue (generator agent) -> validate (mechanical) -> cross_check (different-model judge) -> write_case
                       ^---- retry up to 2 times on validation failure, then discard
```

- **pick_base_code:** choose a function or hunk from a sample repo; check it parses.
- **seed_issue:** given category, difficulty and target size, return modified code, changed line numbers and the exact inserted quote. Instructions: minimal textbook-level flaw, same style, no hint comments, never working exploit code, never real credentials or hostnames. Prompt skeleton lives in `evals/factory/prompts/seed_issue.v1.md`.
- **validate (no model):** the file still parses (`ast.parse`); the diff applies cleanly; claimed lines are inside the diff; the quote is on those lines; where a tool covers the category (bandit for injection, subprocess, weak crypto, TLS; the repo's own secret scanner for secrets), the tool fires on the seeded code.
- **cross_check:** ask a different model family one narrow question: does this diff contain a flaw of category X at lines Y to Z? Require agreement. On disagreement write the candidate to `evals/datasets/<version>/review_queue/` for audit and exclude it from evaluation instead of assigning a label.
- **Mutation cases:** use `ast` to produce mutations, run the sample repo's tests, keep only mutations that fail at least one test.
- **Fallback without an LLM:** each of the 12 security categories also has a template-based seeder (string templates over small code patterns) so v0.1 can be built with no model access. Mark `generated_by: template`.

Commands: `python -m evals.factory build --version v0.1`, `python -m evals.factory validate --version v0.1`, `python -m evals.factory stats --version v0.1`.

## Quality control

1. Mechanical validators on every case.
2. Cross-model check on every seeded case (skipped and logged when no model is available).
3. De-duplication: drop near-identical cases (normalized-diff similarity above 0.9).
4. Unresolved cross-check disagreements stay in the build's review queue and are excluded from the dataset until mechanical or cross-model evidence resolves them.
5. Mechanical validators, provenance, and per-case hashes are checked before the manifest is written.

## Splits, canaries, versions

Dev and test split by hash (DECISIONS #19). The canary set is 15 must-catch cases chosen across categories, tier `canary`, frozen. Versions live in `evals/datasets/v0.1/`, `v0.2/`; never edit a case after a baseline uses it; add a new version. Report results by source so contamination and synthetic-versus-real differences are visible.

## Size plan for v0.1 (about 150 base cases)

48 seeded security (12 categories x 4), 20 hard negatives, 30 presumed clean, 12 mutation bugs, 10 test gaps, 12 injection wrappers, plus optional reversed fixes. Variants and verifier attacks are generated on top and reported separately.

## Safety

Secrets in the dataset are always synthetic. Seeded flaws are minimal textbook patterns for testing a defensive reviewer. Never generate working exploit code.
